name: Axial Spondyloarthritis / Ankylosing Spondylitis
summary: Regular exercise, mobility, posture, aerobic fitness and strength are central alongside rheumatology medical management.

redFlags: New neurological symptoms after even minor trauma
firstSteps: Measure spinal mobility, posture, chest expansion, hip/shoulder ROM and function.
Ask about eye symptoms, fracture history and neurological change.
selfCare: Smoking cessation support through appropriate services when relevant

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Exercise is a long-term management strategy alongside rheumatology medical care.
do: Measure spinal mobility, posture, chest expansion, hip/shoulder ROM and function.
Ask about eye symptoms, fracture history and neurological change.
Assess: Spinal mobility and chest expansion

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Maintain spinal mobility, chest expansion, strength and aerobic fitness.
dose: Spinal mobility: 5–10 reps per direction daily.
Chest expansion/breathing: 5–10 deep controlled breaths × several bouts/day.
Aerobic: build toward 20–30+ minutes most days.
moveOn: Increase aerobic and resistance dose gradually

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Forceful manipulation can be dangerous in ankylosed/osteoporotic spines.
when: Increase aerobic and resistance dose gradually
do: Smoking cessation support through appropriate services when relevant
dose: Progress strength/aerobic load while preserving daily mobility.
Modify during inflammatory flares but avoid prolonged inactivity.

manual: Gentle mobility techniques may be used in appropriate patients

Avoid high-force manipulation where ankylosis, osteoporosis or fracture risk exists.
modalities: Passive modalities should not replace regular exercise
progression: Increase aerobic and resistance dose gradually

mistakes: Missing fracture risk after minor trauma.
education: Teach urgent review for new neurological symptoms after trauma.
Coordinate with rheumatology for inflammatory control.
escalation: Rheumatology/medical review for uncontrolled inflammatory symptoms, suspected fracture or extra-articular complications
